questions.question: Which pattern best fits osteoarthritis?
choices: Activity-related pain with brief stiffness after rest
Persistent fever and hot swollen joint
questions.explanation: OA commonly causes activity-related pain, brief stiffness after rest, reduced range of motion, and gradual structural joint change.

questions.question: Which feature supports inflammatory arthritis such as RA?
choices: Prolonged morning stiffness with persistent swollen joints
Pain only after a single trauma
questions.explanation: RA is immune-mediated synovitis and commonly presents with persistent inflammatory joint swelling and prolonged morning stiffness.

questions.question: What is the mechanism of gout?
choices: Monosodium urate crystals provoke intense inflammation
questions.explanation: Urate crystal deposition triggers acute innate inflammatory activation and severe monoarthritis.

questions.question: What is the priority for a hot swollen joint with fever and inability to bear weight?
choices: Urgently evaluate for septic arthritis including synovial-fluid assessment
Wait for outpatient imaging next month
questions.explanation: Septic arthritis can rapidly destroy cartilage and cause sepsis. Prompt evaluation and synovial-fluid analysis are central when suspected.

questions.question: Why is a normal CRP insufficient to exclude septic arthritis?
choices: No clinical or blood test alone reliably excludes it
questions.explanation: Clinical features and blood tests cannot reliably exclude septic arthritis; aspiration is recommended promptly when suspicion exists.

questions.question: Which back-pain symptom is an emergency red flag?
questions.explanation: Saddle anesthesia and bladder/bowel dysfunction can indicate cauda equina syndrome and require urgent emergency assessment.

questions.question: A high serum urate during acute monoarthritis means:
choices: It supports context but does not confirm gout or exclude infection
questions.explanation: Serum urate alone does not diagnose acute gout. Crystal disease and infection can coexist; evaluate a concerning hot joint safely.

questions.question: Why is early RA referral important?
choices: Persistent synovitis can cause irreversible cartilage and bone damage
questions.explanation: Ongoing immune synovitis can cause erosions, deformity, and disability. Early assessment and disease control are important.

questions.question: A patient with a prosthetic knee has acute warmth, pain, swelling, and fever. What is the safest disposition?
questions.explanation: A prosthetic joint with acute inflammatory symptoms and fever raises concern for joint infection and needs urgent evaluation.

questions.question: Which triad best describes a safe acute-joint evaluation?
choices: Pattern, infection risk/stability, and need for aspiration
Pain score, plain radiograph, and serum urate alone
Joint location, rheumatoid factor, and a trial of NSAIDs
ESR/CRP, an autoimmune panel, and routine follow-up
questions.explanation: Assess joint pattern, systemic/infection risk and stability, then determine whether urgent synovial-fluid analysis is needed.
